title.narrative: Strengthening capacities for biodiversity conservation & sustainability Ecuador

description.narrative: Ecuador as part of the Andean countries share a significant diversity within numerous ecosystems in four regions: the Andes, the Amazon, the Coast and the Galapagos islands. The country has a great number of indigenous communities mostly in the highlands and the amazon, which represents a good source of unique ancestral knowledge, that needs to be duly incorporated in public policies for climate change mitigation, disaster risk reduction, water management and, in general, sustainable development. In the last biennium, the Quito Office organized a regional workshop, on indigenous and local knowledge and its role in scientific and environmental policy. In this context, the office will continue working to raise awareness and strengthen the visibility of young and indigenous voices, working with those minority groups in order to involve them in the projects and initiatives. It is essential to strengthen scientific knowledge, to develop tools for disseminating that knowledge, sharing data and using data for decision-making in Ecuador. This in turn, will strengthen public policies for biodiversity conservation and the promotion of a better living in harmony between communities and nature. The existence of Biosphere reserves in Ecuador, as well as the growing interest in the UNESCO Global Geopark network enhances multi-stakeholder governance tools and encourages the production of scientific research for improving management of natural resources and ecosystem restauration. Galapagos, as an emblematic case, holds a great presence of scientific institutions, NGOs and international cooperation; however, it faces many challenges related to illegal exploitation of natural resources, species trafficking, invasive species, water-borne issues, among others. In the framework of the MAB programme, UNESCO Quito supported Galapagos BR with the development of a centralized digital platform that consolidates georeferenced data, scientific research and other contents from different sources. This is to promote a broader dissemination of information, as well as the local population’s involvement in the conservation and protection of Galapagos. The Regional Government of Galapagos, together with the scientific community, has identified that youth involvement and awareness is insufficient, as Galapagos has been positioned as a tourist destination. In this context, the Quito Office will continue supporting educational and awareness-raising activities for Galapagos and other BR in the country, especially through the involvement of youth. The creation of a Transnational Biosphere Marine Reserve that would be one of the biggest protected marine areas in the world, covering the so-called Migravía supported by the governments of Ecuador, Colombia, Costa Rica and Panama during COP26, it´s in an ongoing process and we will continue supporting the nomination folder by providing technical assistance.
